title: 나도 날아가요?  (Am I Getting Fired Too?)

segments.t: Following Kim Tae-ho back to his office, Ra Joon-mo anxiously asks if he is losing his job along with his cast, then reflects on how lonely a cancelled show feels. Listen for the workplace slang for getting axed, and the expression for 'a funeral home'.
나는 어떻게 돼요? 나도 날아가요?
넌 안 날아가.
일단 멤버만 새로 짜서 다시 들어가보란 말이야.
언제부터요?
뭘 언제부터야, 지금 당장이지!
지금 제일 급한 거는 멤버들한테 빨리 알리는 거야.
방송 시작할 때 보면 돌잔치 같죠?
방송 막 내릴 때 보면 상갓집 같아요.
Let's unpack the eight lines of Joon-mo's talk with Tae-ho.
나는 어떻게 돼요? 나도 날아가요?

'What happens to me? Am I getting blown away too?' First comes the question 'what becomes of me?'. Then comes a word that literally means 'to fly away in the wind' — colorful workplace slang for losing your post! The word doubles the.
넌 안 날아가.

'You aren't getting blown away.' Tae-ho reassures him with a casual contraction meaning 'as for you', followed by the negated word. Placing the negative marker right before the action flips 'fly away' into 'you're staying put' The word doubles the.
일단 멤버만 새로 짜서 다시 들어가보란 말이야.

'Just put together a new cast first and jump back in.' It opens with an word meaning 'first of all' or 'for starters', a lifesaver when breaking big tasks into step one. Korean variety shows use a loanword for their regular cast, paired with a phrase meaning to assemble a fresh lineup It comes from this.
언제부터요?
'Starting when?' Combine the question word for 'when' with the word for 'from' or 'starting at', and tack on the polite ending. Three words in English, one compact Korean chunk The word doubles the.
뭘 언제부터야, 지금 당장이지!

'What do you mean starting when, right this second!' Echoing a question with a dismissive 'what...' brushes it aside as obvious: 'what do you mean, when?!'. Then pairing 'now' with 'immediately' delivers 'right this instant!' Notice the word for.
지금 제일 급한 거는 멤버들한테 빨리 알리는 거야.

'The most urgent thing right now is telling the cast members quickly.' The subject phrase means 'the most urgent thing', built on the word for 'urgent'. Then come the word for 'quickly' and a word meaning to let people know official news We built from this.
방송 시작할 때 보면 돌잔치 같죠?

'When a show starts, it looks like a first-birthday party, right?' Turning to the documentary crew, Joon-mo compares a launch to Korea's joyful celebration of a baby's first birthday, where guests crowd in with blessings Swap in this word.
방송 막 내릴 때 보면 상갓집 같아요.

'When the curtain comes down on a show, it feels like a funeral home.' Here he uses the idiom for 'bringing down a stage curtain'. Against that joyful first-birthday celebration, he sets a house in mourning — and Tae-ho loves the metaphor so much he tells the crew not to edit it out! Swap in this word. Now let's listen to the whole conversation in Tae-ho's office again.
나는 어떻게 돼요? 나도 날아가요?
넌 안 날아가.
일단 멤버만 새로 짜서 다시 들어가보란 말이야.
언제부터요?
뭘 언제부터야, 지금 당장이지!
지금 제일 급한 거는 멤버들한테 빨리 알리는 거야.
방송 시작할 때 보면 돌잔치 같죠?
방송 막 내릴 때 보면 상갓집 같아요.

You learned workplace slang for losing a post, how to ask 'starting when?', the emphatic phrase for 'right this instant', and the contrast between a first-birthday celebration and a funeral home. Let's head backstage at Music Bank!
또 만나요!
